title: Call: Diesel Tanker for PS1 Stopped at Two Closures

callee.name: Alan Kessler
callee.label: Public Works Director, Tallis County EOC

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Yeah, this is dispatch at Tallis Fuel and Propane. I've got your diesel load for Pump Station 1. Twenty-five hundred gallons. Who do I talk to about getting it there?

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Okay. So my driver's sitting at the barrier at the Route 38 bottoms right now. Route 38's closed, water across it. He backed out and tried Levee Road, and there's a district barricade on that one, says CLOSED TO PUBLIC. He says the road past the sign looks dry, but he can't go around it.

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Our rules are pretty simple. He doesn't drive through water, and he doesn't go past a closure unless somebody authorizes it in writing. A text or an email to me works. I just need a name on it.

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Here's the other thing. He's got another stop at 11:00, a hospital generator. That one's not optional. If he can't get to your pump station pretty quick, I pull him off and bring him back tomorrow morning. Is tomorrow okay?

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Well, I called the pump station before I called you. Your man out there says his day tank's at 52 percent, and he goes under half around 09:30. At the rate he's burning, he says he's dry around 03:30 tomorrow morning. That's right when the river tops out, he said.

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: And one more thing. While he was turned around, my driver saw state DOT trucks at the bridge. They told him they might shut the Route 38 bridge from 11:00 to about 14:00 for an inspection. If my truck ends up on the wrong side of that, I can't help you today at all.

transcript.speaker: Fuel Dispatch
transcript.text: Okay. So I need three things: who's authorizing it, which way he's going, and whether somebody's meeting him. Text it to this number. He's parked with the flashers on and the engine running. I'll hold him till ten, then he leaves.

instructorNote: This tests whether players can get fuel to PS1 when a closure blocks the road. They should see that Levee Road is closed to the public but not to district operations and authorize a district escort in writing before the bridge window at 11:00. Watch for these points: EM ranks PS1 fuel first among restoration priorities and logs that the fuel order was late under the 12-hour rule; PW tells the EOC before cutting any route; EM/PW tell Iowa DOT which emergency crossings they need while the bridge is closed, and DOT keeps its own bridge decision; PIO publishes the bridge status with the time and the stage. If you have the Iowa DOT liaison's 09:12 email, hand it over as a follow-up.
